subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact Private Mode contract should OpenClaw guarantee across context reads, transcript/session storage, memory/compaction, plugin artifacts, channel history, logs, attachments, and Control UI state?
rationale: The requested behavior creates a user-visible privacy/security boundary spanning several owners, and current main has no single session mode or field that downstream paths can enforce safely.

options.title: Design a shared private-session contract
options.body: Add one additive private-session mode with explicit no-context/no-persist semantics that every storage, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path must honor.

options.title: Narrow to context suppression only
options.body: Ship a smaller, clearly named context-suppression mode if maintainers do not want to promise no durable history or memory writes yet.

options.title: Defer with documented mitigations
options.body: Keep the issue open and document current partial controls such as contextInjection:"never" without claiming private sessions.

recommendation.title: Design a shared private-session contract
recommendation.body: Add one additive private-session mode with explicit no-context/no-persist semantics that every storage, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path must honor.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior source-backed review already treated this as the canonical private-mode tracker and the unresolved choice is a product/security contract.
